headline: High: TREK’s browser/MCP and shared file surfaces create medium-to-high risks of leakage, prompt injection, and cascading errors when paired with Taipy’s data-engineering workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK can run browsers and use MCP, and it has collaborative real-time sessions plus file surfaces; Taipy is a data-engineering tool that may ingest outputs into workflows. No direct shared channel is documented, so the interaction is inferred, but the browser/MCP path makes instruction-hijack plausible.
conditions: IF TREK ingests web or MCP content into prompts without provenance checks, injection becomes actionable.
IF Taipy consumes TREK-generated text or files as trusted instructions, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Disable MCP for untrusted sources during paired runs.
Require provenance tags on all browser-sourced content.
Route TREK outputs through a human review step before Taipy consumes them.
Use separate workspaces for browser-derived artifacts.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK explicitly touches sensitive classes like API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and documents, while Taipy has network egress none and no data classes listed. The pair still shares a plausible leakage path through TREK’s files/uploads and collaborative surfaces; Taipy could expose imported artifacts if the workspace is shared.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or uploaded files, sensitive TREK data can flow into Taipy processing.
IF TREK stores secrets or reservations in ./uploads/ or ./data/travel.db and Taipy reads them, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Keep Taipy and TREK on separate volumes.
Restrict TREK uploads to non-sensitive test data.
Mask secrets before any cross-agent handoff.
Audit file permissions on ./data/ and ./uploads/.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and DLP scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Taipy shows no write or network surfaces beyond none egress, while TREK has allowlisted egress, browser use, MCP, and collaborative multi-instance support. Overlap exists mainly if both are pointed at the same files or shared mutable resources; no direct same-dir write conflict is documented, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same filesystem path, write conflicts can occur.
IF TREK and Taipy share a mutable database or git checkout, concurrent edits may race.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Avoid shared git working trees.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Run one agent at a time for mutable resources.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative travel planner with AI built in, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream workflows. Taipy is a data-engineering/automation tool that can operationalize inputs; if it consumes TREK outputs without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect plans or actions.
conditions: IF Taipy uses TREK-generated itineraries, budgets, or reservations without validation, downstream errors propagate.
IF TREK’s AI output is fed directly into automation steps, false facts can be acted on.
mitigations: Add a validation step before Taipy acts on TREK output.
Require source links for itinerary facts.
Compare critical fields against original reservations.
Limit automation to read-only summaries.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation and confidence gating.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK touches country visit history, documents, photos, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while Taipy is a general data-engineering tool with no stated residency controls. The pair creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated travel data is processed without matching retention or residency guarantees; Taipy’s side lacks documented controls.
conditions: IF TREK data includes EU PII or sensitive travel records and Taipy processes them outside the required residency boundary, compliance risk occurs.
IF retention or deletion requests must be honored across both systems and only TREK supports them, mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify travel records before cross-agent processing.
Keep regulated data out of Taipy unless residency is confirmed.
Document retention rules for shared artifacts.
Purge logs containing identifiers after each run.
requires-engineering: align both systems to a common compliance policy.
